description:
FILED s537b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-11) while doing #314 F-F (state containers).  PRE-EXISTING: main 3d524ad7 gives the same answer.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; scratch/s537b/pr/m1i.pl in the s537b worktree):

    use feature 'state';
    state $s = 5; print eval('$s'), "\n";
    for (1..2) { state $t = 10; $t++; print eval('$t'), "\n" }

perl:  5 / 11 / 12
PCL:   (three empty lines)

WHY: the state SOURCE rewrite (`Parser2::_rewrite_state_prepass` / `_state_rewrite_site`) renames the declaration to a package cell `$s__state__N` and every use to it, so the eval text's `$s` resolves through p-eval-lex-lookup to the package global `$main::s`.  Only the CLASSIC route (a scalar statement at the TOP level of a named sub's block, #401) registers an eval-capture pair (`_eval_state_captures`).  The anon-sub route (`do { my $s__state__N; ... sub {...} }`) is let-bound but its alist key is the mangled name (`_eval_lexical_alist`'s skey does not strip `__state__N`).

A CONTAINER of the same routes (`state @a`, `state %h`, s537b) REFUSES instead when a later string eval may name it (`_state_eval_blocker`, rule 12) -- so this task is the scalar's residue, and fixing it lets the container refusal go.

FIX DIRECTION (not designed): a per-site pair for the cell, block-scoped like M5's `_eval_block_cells`: register `"$s" -> $s__state__N` in `_let_bound_vars` at the DECLARING statement (the prepass reparses the document, so the statement has to be found again after it -- by the cell token, the first in document order), strip `__state__(e<hex>_)?N` in the alist key, and keep it across `_lower_sub`'s wipe like `_eval_block_cells`.  A block lowered through the v1 seam (map/grep blocks) never reaches `_lower_block_1`: a pending pair must die there (rule 12), as `_pending_eval_caps` does.  Then delete `_state_eval_blocker`.

BAR: corpus-diff + wide emission-ab (every state site whose scope holds a string eval moves), gate, sweep (name resolution), the gate-SET scan if a refusal goes.
subject: A `state $x` outside a named sub's own statement (file level, a file-level loop or bare block, a nested block of a named sub, a map block) is NOT visible to a string eval by its name -- `state $s = 5; print eval '$s'` prints EMPTY (the package global), perl 5 -- SILENT WRONG, pre-existing
